A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCENT study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable despite repagination and revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations and experiments on extreme classification, partial AUC maximization, CLIP training, and distributionally robust optimization, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised classification and partial-AUC results in Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: The general SCENT algorithm is retained. Appendix F.4, Algorithm 5 corrects the written CLIP procedure by introducing temperature scaling in the exponentials and dual-normalizer terms in the model gradient. These are substantive pseudocode corrections; the PDFs do not establish a change to the underlying CLIP implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Glint360K and TreeOfLife-10M for extreme classification, imbalanced CIFAR-10/100 for partial AUC, DFN-14M with DataComp evaluation for CLIP, California housing and Abalone for DRO, and the same Gaussian simulation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, but v2 acknowledges a bug in the earlier ASGD (Softplus) implementation for partial AUC and revises that comparison. The new Table 1 compares theoretical properties; it does not introduce additional empirically evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix F.4 substantially revises partial-AUC tuning across methods, datasets, temperatures, and optimizers. The model learning-rate range changes from 1e-5–1e-3 to 1e-4–1e-2, Softplus rho from 1e-11–1e-7 to 1e-5–1e-1, and SOX gamma from 0.9–0.99 to 0.3–0.9. Selected settings are extensively replaced in v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 4, while data construction and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing optimizer robustness analysis is revised through updated extreme-classification and partial-AUC curves with momentum in Appendix F.1, Figures 4–5. No new ablation or robustness question is introduced, and the Gaussian comparisons remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random-seed runs with averages and error bars for Section 5, and means and standard deviations across ten runs for DRO. Revised uncertainty bands do not establish a change in the reporting procedure or run counts.

E6.justification: Figures 3 and 5 replace the partial-AUC trajectories across methods, materially changing convergence curves and performance gaps under revised settings. Figures 2 and 4 also revise ASGD (Softplus) classification curves. The broad SCENT/SOX advantage remains, while Gaussian results, CLIP Figure 7, and the DRO table are retained. The partial-AUC changes are not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the sign in Lemma B.5, restores missing learning-rate factors in Appendix A, expands Corollary B.8's proof, and adds the KL-DRO derivation in Appendix F.3. The main convergence results and Appendix E bounds remain. Some edits introduce errors, notably printing E[z]^2 instead of E[z^2] in Section 4.2's moment-ratio definition.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly adds mitigation of stochastic variance to the stated contribution, which previously emphasized exponentially large smoothness. The principal claims about SCENT, its convex O(1/sqrt(T)) rate, dual-update advantages, and application performance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The expanded conclusion explicitly identifies the absence of nonconvex theory and SCENT's inability to maintain per-sample dual variables when n is infinite, suggesting neural prediction as future work. Section 4.3 adds an explanation of why Euclidean proximal updates retain the unfavorable variance factor, and Section 3 softens the asserted slowdown from 'will' to 'may'.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SCENT code-availability link and identifies TAMU ACES and NCSA Delta computing resources. Appendix F.4 revises partial-AUC hyperparameter documentation and corrects CLIP pseudocode. Most other implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Song et al. (2020) on active class selection and Chadha et al. (2022) on stochastic proximal methods, clarifies early contributions by Qi and Li, and adds a theoretical comparison table. Most remaining reference changes update bibliographic information for the same works.

P1.justification: There are local language corrections, clearer encoder descriptions and proof explanations, an expanded 'Conclusion and Discussion', and new acknowledgments. Conference publication text replaces the preprint notice. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the theoretical comparison Table 1 and redraws partial-AUC Figures 3 and 5 with revised axis ranges. Existing figures, algorithms, and tables are reflowed, with the partial-AUC hyperparameter table placed on its own page. The overall visual design is retained.

improvement.justification: Addressing the acknowledged baseline implementation bug, correcting CLIP pseudocode, adding code-access information, and stating meaningful applicability limits improve empirical credibility and reproducibility. The gains are limited by the largely retained scientific contribution and newly introduced equation errors, including the moment-ratio misprint in Section 4.2.
